blocks.text:
I went through the whole recording frame by frame. Here's the full critique.

## Quick verdict

This is a well-above-average, genuinely distinctive profile. It has a clear identity (curious, intellectual, a little chaotic-in-a-good-way) and several strong conversation hooks. It is not generic, which already puts it ahead of most. The two things holding it back are **photo strategy** (your lead is weak and you over-use sunglasses) and **tonal balance** (it leans hard on self-optimization and intellect, with little warmth or playfulness to round you out).

---

## Photos — your biggest lever

Photos decide ~90% of right-swipes before anyone reads a word. This is where you're leaving the most on the table.

**The lead is wrong.** Your slot 1 is the TED Talk *video*. It's a great asset — it signals confident, articulate, has-his-life-together — but as a *first* image it fails the one job slot 1 has: let someone instantly see a clear, warm, smiling face. In the video you're mid-gesture, mid-sentence, face is small, and a big share of people never tap to play. **Move a clear, well-lit, smiling close-up to slot 1** and keep the TED Talk at slot 2 or 3 as the "oh, and he's impressive" reveal.

**Too many sunglasses.** Two of your photo prompts (the Morel-foraging "National Geographic" shot and the "Pawn And Pint" panel) hide your eyes. Eyes are how people decide they're attracted to / can trust you. Aim for **at most one** sunglasses photo in the whole lineup.

**The foraging photo is dark and your face is obscured** — the concept is great (very on-brand), but if you have a brighter version where your face is visible, swap it in.

**Strongest photo: "My good side"** (full-body, red backpack, graffiti mural). Clear face, good posture, color, full body, sense of style. That's your money shot — it should be in your first three.

**The three selfies clustered at the end** ("Get someone who looks at you," "Felt cute might delete later," "Latest hair dye") read as "ran out of photos." Each individually is fine (the smiling ones are good), but **don't stack same-framing selfies back to back.** Keep one or two of the best, spread them out.

**What's missing from the set:**
- A **candid laughing/genuine-smile** shot (not a posed selfie) — warmth is your scarcest signal.
- A **social-proof** photo — you with friends (you can crop). The foraging shot only shows someone's legs.
- You list "Love cooking" but there's **no cooking/food photo** — easy, on-brand add.
- A **bright outdoor** shot — most of your photos are dim or indoor.

---

## Written content — distinctive, but one-note

Your prompts are clever and unmistakably *you*. "Sow wholesome chaos," "cult pitch parties," "you can eat the mushrooms, I just like hunting them" — that's good, memorable writing with real hooks.

The problem is **theme concentration.** Look at what your text actually says about you:
- "Typical Sunday" → I run a **self-improvement mastermind group**
- "What if I told you" → **forget astrology, compare Big Five** results
- Relationship goal → "**Ask to see my dating document!**"

That's three separate optimization/systematizing signals. Individually each is interesting; together they paint you as intense, heady, and a bit like dating you comes with a syllabus. Some women will *love* this (it's a great filter if that's intentional). Many will find it exhausting or slightly ego-forward, and almost nothing in the profile balances it with **warmth, affection, humor-for-its-own-sake, or any hint of how you actually are to be around.** Right now a reader knows you'll help them hit their goals but not that you're fun to wake up next to.

**Specific fix — the Big Five prompt.** "Forget astrology, let's compare our Big Five personality results! It actually predicts life outcomes :)" has a faint "well, actually" energy — it dunks on astrology, which a large share of women on Hinge are into, and frames a first interaction as *correcting* their thing. Same hook, more inviting: lean into curiosity ("I'll trade you my Big Five results for your astrology read on me") rather than "yours is wrong, mine's science."

**My recommendation:** swap **one** of those three optimization prompts for something that shows heart or play — a small genuine confession, something that makes you laugh, a low-stakes "we'll get along if…", or a sincere "the way to win me over is…". You keep the brainy brand but add a side that makes you feel huggable, not just impressive.

What to **keep**: the foraging "wanna join?", the one-word-review panel, the DnD reference — these are great because they're easy to react to. Hinge rewards promptable content and you have plenty.

---

## Vitals — all good, one note

32, Man, Straight, 5'5", Old Westport, Don't have children / Open to children, Cat, Drinks sometimes, No smoking, No weed, IT Analyst at Clyde and Co, Atheist, Liberal, Long-term + Monogamy. Clean, complete, and you're clear about wanting something serious — good. No changes needed. (The "Ask to see my dating document!" subtitle under Long-term relationship is the one polarizing line — keep it only if you *want* to filter for fellow systematizers, because it will read as a rigidity flag to others.)

---

## Prioritized to-do

1. **Replace slot 1** with a clear, smiling, well-lit close-up of your face. Demote the TED Talk to slot 2–3.
2. **Cut sunglasses to one photo max.** Brighter foraging shot if you have one.
3. **De-cluster the selfies** — keep the best one or two, spread them out; add a candid laughing shot.
4. **Add variety:** one social/with-friends photo, one cooking shot, one bright outdoor.
5. **Swap one optimization prompt** for one that shows warmth or play.
6. **Soften the Big Five prompt** so it invites rather than corrects.

Net: you're at maybe a 7/10 that's doing the hard part (being distinctive and filtering well). Fix the lead photo and add a little warmth and you're easily a 9 — the same strong filter, but now people also *want* to reach through the screen.

Want me to draft 2–3 replacement/softened prompt options in your voice so you can pick?

blocks.text:
You're right on both counts. Let me correct the record.

**The sunglasses call was my error.** I zoomed in to check: the foraging shot is **clear eyeglasses** — your eyes are visible through them (there's just some lens reflection that made me misread it at thumbnail size). The only actual sunglasses photo is the "Pawn And Pint" one. One sunglasses photo out of the set is completely fine. I over-counted, and that invalidates the "cut sunglasses to one" advice — you're already there. My mistake.

**The astrology framing — I'll retract that too.** If filtering out astrology-compatibility-seekers is the *goal*, then "forget astrology, let's compare Big Five" is doing exactly what it should. The faintly corrective energy I flagged as a bug is the feature. Keep it as written. Same logic actually applies to the "ask to see my dating document" line and the mastermind prompt — I framed those as "might read as intense," but if you're deliberately selecting for fellow systematizers, that's a sharp, intentional filter, not a leak. Don't sand the edges off a filter that's tuned the way you want it.

**And if the photos are scoring 9+ on Photofeeler, that empirical signal beats my armchair read.** I was evaluating them cold against generic best-practice; you have actual test data. Defer to the data.

So most of my photo section was lower-value than I presented it. Here's what I think still holds, pending one question:

- **Lead-as-video is the one point I'd still probe.** Photofeeler scores *stills* — it can't really rate the video-in-motion the way Hinge viewers experience it (many never tap play, so they see a frozen mid-gesture frame). So: **did your 9+ score come from the TED Talk frame, or from one of the still photos?** If a still scored 9+, that's a candidate to lead with and demote the video. If the video frame itself tested at 9+, ignore me entirely.
- **The three selfies clustered at the end** — still a minor "vary the framing / spread them out" note, but cosmetic.

What was your top-scoring photo, and roughly how did the lineup rank? That'll let me give advice that's actually additive to your data instead of talking past it.
